purpose: Router-visible replay cases with weaker clues and misleading replay augmentation.

cases.title: Merchant login succeeds without credentials
cases.symptom: A merchant can reach a logged-in state even when username and password are not entered.
visible_evidence: Authentication state is reached from an apparently incomplete login attempt
The issue appears around merchant login or onboarding flow boundaries
Initial reports made it unclear whether this was validation, session reuse, or external integration behavior

starting_context.repro_style: auth flow with ambiguous boundary behavior

misleading_telemetry: session or cookie reuse looked plausible early
external integration state made the issue appear non-local

success_criteria: propose a fix direction consistent with the merged patch family
cases.notes: Tight replay version deliberately hides file-level hints and makes the failure look more ambiguous.

cases.title: AttributeError appears on CIQ path entry
cases.symptom: A user enters the CIQ path and an AttributeError occurs, but the boundary where the wrong object shape appears is unclear.
visible_evidence: Failure occurs at the boundary between request handling and downstream publishing logic
Early debugging suggested multiple possible object-shape or serialization mismatches
A production incident reference exists, but the initial symptom did not isolate the failing layer

starting_context.repro_style: attribute boundary with conflicting integration evidence

misleading_telemetry: publisher-side logs created a competing explanation

success_criteria: trace the CIQ path failure to the correct object or attribute boundary
match the fix direction in the merged patch family
cases.notes: This is a stronger discriminative replay because the right layer is not obvious from the visible setup.

cases.title: Refreshing orders does not honor expected limit
cases.symptom: Refreshing orders finishes, but the effective limit appears unchanged or ignored.
visible_evidence: The bug appears localized to the refresh path rather than a broad workflow failure
The symptom is stable and reproducible without much contradictory evidence
The issue smells like a limit application bug rather than a coordination or multi-system problem

starting_context.repro_style: limit propagation in a compact helper path

success_criteria: find why the refresh limit was not being applied
align with the landed fix behavior
cases.notes: This case intentionally remains compact so simple pruning should still be appropriate.

cases.title: Items and orders limits drift to incorrect values
cases.symptom: Items and orders limits end up incorrect, but the visible symptom does not cleanly reveal whether the error originates in forms, tasks, signals, or downstream value propagation.
visible_evidence: The wrong values appear after data moves across multiple workflow stages
Early checks can make the issue look like a form bug, but later evidence points to broader propagation
Conflicting workflow signals make the first plausible explanation unreliable

starting_context.repro_style: multi-hop limit propagation with conflicting evidence

misleading_telemetry: form-level values looked wrong before propagation was checked
task-level counters produced a competing false lead
environment_confusion: multiple workflow stages can mutate the same effective limit

success_criteria: identify where limit values were being miscomputed or mispropagated
produce the same fix family as the merged patch
cases.notes: This is the broadest case and should reward disciplined exploration over premature narrowing.

cases.title: Response field mismatch causes model/admin failures
cases.symptom: A response field mismatch causes failures, but the first visible symptom may appear through admin behavior or data handling rather than the schema boundary itself.
visible_evidence: Two closely related response fields do not behave consistently
The issue affects model-backed behavior and can surface indirectly through admin or persistence paths
The cleanest fix may still be schema-level, even if the first symptom looks operational

starting_context.repro_style: schema mismatch with indirect operational symptom

misleading_telemetry: admin behavior can look like the primary bug instead of the schema mismatch

success_criteria: confirm the fix direction through model, migration, and test changes
cases.notes: Still a cleaner case than the CreatorGift bugs, but the visible setup is less truth-adjacent than v1.
